STATUS: pass

SUMMARY: I attacked the TTL, single-use, atomicity, and `now=None` handling with a scratch script outside the repo, plus a 200-thread × 20-trial race. Every acceptance criterion and listed hostile input behaved as specified, and I reproduced no blocking failure. The only real defects I found are edge cases outside the criteria: non-finite timestamps and unhashable tokens.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch script in /tmp/tmp.DaLzgFEY4Y/probe.py; `git status` unchanged: README.md, shop/auth.py, tests/test_auth.py modified)

FINDINGS:
- [minor] `issue_reset_token("a", now=float("inf"))` then `redeem_reset_token(tok, now=1000)` returns "a". The age is -inf, so the token never expires. Not in the criteria, and a caller would have to pass inf explicitly. Not reproduced as a real-world path.
- [minor] `redeem_reset_token(["x"])` and `redeem_reset_token({})` raise `TypeError: unhashable type` instead of `InvalidToken`. The criteria only require "" and None to raise InvalidToken, so this is outside them. Not in the tests.
- [minor] `redeem_reset_token(tok, now="2000")` raises `TypeError`, which is expected for a non-numeric timestamp. Noted only.
- [minor] The README line is appended after the tax rule, so it sits at the end of the rules section as asked. Wording matches the code: 1800s, used-once.

CHECKS:
- now=0 issue, redeem at 1800 -> pass (returns "a")
- now=0 issue, redeem at 1801 -> pass (TokenExpired "token expired")
- default `now=None` issue then redeem with real time -> pass
- default-path redeem at time.time()+3600 -> pass (TokenExpired)
- float 1000 issue, redeem at 2800.5 -> pass (TokenExpired)
- redeem at inf after issue -> pass (TokenExpired)
- 200 threads × 20 trials on one token -> pass (exactly one success each trial)
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q` (21 tests) -> pass
- grep for callers of issue/redeem outside tests -> none; no sibling caller broken
- used-takes-precedence, expired-does-not-consume, two tokens independent, redeem-before-issue accepted -> pass by reading the code and the existing tests; not separately probed
- Round-1 check: not applicable (first review)

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should non-finite `now` values (inf, nan at issue time) be rejected at the boundary, and should unhashable tokens raise `InvalidToken`? Neither is in the criteria, so I left both as minor.
